receipt.public_excerpt: On each dataset, we show that standard training yields substantially lower out-of-distribution than in-distribution performance.

evidence_items.explanation: WILDS compares within-distribution and shifted performance across ten datasets covering varied applications. The consistent substantial gaps support the claimed recurring weakness.

receipt.public_excerpt: However, when generalization requires systematic compositional skills (as in the "dax" example above), RNNs fail spectacularly.

evidence_items.explanation: The study tests several recurrent-network variants and reports successful generalization when training and test commands differ little, followed by failures on systematic compositional tests. It supports the distinction Marcus describes in a controlled setting.

receipt.public_excerpt: Our results show how a standard neural network architecture, optimized for its compositional skills, can mimic human systematic generalization in a head-to-head comparison.

evidence_items.explanation: Meta-learning produces successful systematic generalization and improves performance on several compositional benchmarks. This limits any categorical reading of neural-network incapacity, but a successful exception does not refute the stated tendency.
